en.title: Zolostays OA #2: Trapping Rain Water
en.description: Given the non-negative heights of n adjacent bars, each of width 1, compute the total units of water these bars can trap after rain. There are no extra walls at the ends, so water can flow out. The original snapshot's text is truncated, but the starter explicitly references LC42; this site completed the width and water-trapping definitions from that official statement, and the two original examples and full constraints agree with the official version.
en.input: Input n, followed by n heights, separated by whitespace. Full original range 1≤n≤20000, 0≤height[i]≤100000; empty arrays are not accepted. The standard input is this site's adaptation of the array parameter.
en.output: Output the total units of rain water trapped, as an exact integer with no modulo.
en.explanation: The two original examples keep 6 and 9; the third example [2,0,2]→2 is added by this site. The source text was truncated rather than defining different rules; the completion is based on https://leetcode.com/problems/trapping-rain-water/description/, which the original starter explicitly references, not merely guessed from the title.
hints: The water level at each position is limited by the smaller of the tallest walls on its left and right.
Computing prefix and suffix maximums first gives an independent linear solution.
With two pointers, each step settles the end whose lower boundary is already known.
